title: IShowSpeed Screaming
blurb: IShowSpeed screaming — the most powerful lungs in streaming, captured mid-eruption. Speed's screams are their own genre: joy, rage, and jumpscare reaction all delivered at identical, catastrophic volume. Use it for hype moments, ambushes, and any situation that deserves total vocal commitment. One of the defining streamer sounds of the era, from the man who made screaming an art form.
origin: From IShowSpeed's streams — the most famous scream in streaming.

title: RUN (Vine)
blurb: The RUN sound — the panicked command from Vine that became the internet's universal evacuation alarm. Something bad has been spotted and there is exactly one correct response. Play it over animals charging, plans collapsing, or the moment someone's mom counts to three. The urgency is absolute and the comedy is in how fast everyone complies.
origin: From the classic Vine clip; the internet's evacuation order.

title: We'll Be Right Back
blurb: WE'LL BE RIGHT BACK — the smash-cut escape hatch from The Eric Andre Show. When a moment becomes too chaotic, too awkward, or too incriminating to continue, this sting plus an implied freeze-frame ends the broadcast immediately. It's the perfect edit-out for conversations going off the rails. Nothing gets resolved; we simply cut to commercial.
origin: The cutaway sting popularized by The Eric Andre Show meme edits.

title: Tom Scream
blurb: The Tom scream — the shrieking AAAAH of cartoon history's most punished cat. Eighty years of Jerry-related disasters distilled into one wail. It's the perfect overreaction sound: stubbed toes, jump scares, seeing the electricity bill. The scream's vintage theatrical quality makes modern minor inconveniences feel like classic slapstick catastrophes.
origin: Tom's iconic scream from Tom and Jerry.

title: WHAT?! (JonTron)
blurb: JonTron's WHAT?! — the most incredulous syllable on YouTube, delivered with a full-body disbelief that words cannot improve. It's the reaction for statements that break the laws of logic: impossible excuses, cursed food combinations, plot holes in real life. When something defies explanation, this clip demands one anyway. A reaction-image hall-of-famer in audio form.
origin: JonTron's famous incredulous 'WHAT?!' reaction.

title: OH MY GOD (Meme)
blurb: The OH MY GOD meme sound — maximum scandalized energy for revelations of every size. The delivery is theatrical enough to work sincerely on actual shocks and ironically on absolute non-events: someone's wearing the same shirt twice, the meeting ran one minute over, there's no milk. Every group chat needs a designated OH MY GOD, and this is it.
origin: A viral theatrical shock reaction clip.

title: BOI What the Hell, BOI
blurb: 'BOI, what the hell, BOI!' — the double-boi interrogation that surrounds an accusation with pure bewilderment. It's confrontation without menace: whoever hears it knows they've done something inexplicable and must now answer for it. Play it at pets on counters, friends with terrible ideas, and anyone caught mid-shenanigan. The second boi is load-bearing.
origin: A viral double-'boi' confrontation clip.

title: Hello? I'm Under the Water
blurb: 'Hello? I'm under the water. Please help me.' — delivered with the emotional urgency of someone ordering a sandwich. This clip became legendary precisely because the words describe an emergency and the voice describes a Tuesday. It's the sound for crises handled with inexplicable calm: deadlines, floods, life generally. Too much rain. Heh.
origin: From a viral clip of the world's calmest drowning report.

title: Helicopter Helicopter
blurb: HELICOPTER HELICOPTER — the hypnotic chant that colonized TikTok and refused to leave anyone's head. Paired originally with spinning things (all spinning things qualify), it became the soundtrack for rotation of any kind: ceiling fans, figure skaters, office chairs, life spiraling. The 'parakofer parakofer' is not optional; it's the second rotor.
origin: From Fazlija's song 'Helikopter', viral as TikTok's spinning anthem.

title: Cat Laugh
blurb: The laughing cat — a wheezy little feline chuckle attached to the smug cat meme faces of the internet. It's the laugh of someone who watched you fail and feels no obligation to help. Deploy it after fails, bad takes, and anyone dropping their phone on their face. The cat is laughing at you, not with you, and that's the correct dynamic.
origin: The viral laughing-cat meme sound.

title: Rehehehe Laugh
blurb: The rehehehe — a scheming, nasal little laugh that signals mischief in progress. It's the sound of a plan that benefits exactly one person: the laugher. Play it when someone takes the last slice, wins by technicality, or executes a prank they've clearly been saving. Petty victory has an official soundtrack, and it goes rehehehe.
origin: The viral mischievous laugh clip.

title: Explosion (Meme)
blurb: The meme explosion — a full cinematic detonation for moments that deserve one. Arguments ending, secrets dropping, someone hitting reply-all: all technically explosions. This is the clean, big-budget blast for edits that need real impact rather than a cartoon puff. Pair with a slow zoom on someone's face for maximum devastation.
origin: A cinematic explosion for metaphorical detonations everywhere.

title: Screaming Emoji
blurb: The screaming emoji sound — the wail attached to the melting, disintegrating emoji meme. It's digital panic in its purest form: the sound your soul makes when the battery hits 1%, the deadline hits now, or the 'we need to talk' text arrives. Abstract enough for any crisis, dramatic enough for none of them to deserve it.
origin: The scream paired with the disintegrating-emoji meme.

title: UwU
blurb: The UwU sound — weaponized softness. This aggressively adorable little voice clip is deployed both sincerely (rarely) and as a menace (constantly): nothing unsettles a Discord call faster than a grown adult pressing the UwU button in total silence. Use for wholesome moments, cursed moments, and blurring the line between the two.
origin: The internet's official uwu-speak audio.

title: Duck Quack
blurb: A single, assertive duck quack. That's it — and somehow it's never not funny. The quack is comedy's most efficient animal sound: it works as a response, an interruption, a verdict, and a complete argument. Play it in any silence and the silence improves. Science cannot explain the quack's power; Bleepboard simply provides it.
origin: One perfect duck quack.

title: Kissing Sound (Mwah)
blurb: MWAH — the exaggerated kiss sound, from chef's kiss to menace-flirting in Discord calls. It's affection at maximum theatricality: play it to celebrate perfection, greet friends continentally, or make an entire voice chat deeply uncomfortable. The versatility is the point. One button, infinite social chaos, zero actual kissing required.
origin: The classic exaggerated 'mwah' kiss.

title: Snoring (Meme)
blurb: The meme snore — a deep, committed, theatrical snore that communicates one thing: this is boring beyond human endurance. Play it during long stories, meetings that could've been emails, and anyone explaining their fantasy football league. It's the polite society version of leaving. The snorer is asleep; the message is wide awake.
origin: The theatrical bored-snore of meme culture.

title: FlightReacts Laugh
blurb: The FlightReacts laugh — a cackle so distinctive it became its own meme currency. Flight's laugh escalates from wheeze to full system failure, and the internet deploys it wherever composure is being lost in real time. Use it for reactions that start controlled and end in tears. One of streaming culture's most contagious sounds.
origin: FlightReacts' iconic escalating laugh.

title: Biden Soda
blurb: The Biden soda clip — a deep-fried presidential moment that the internet decided was cinema. Part of the genre where world leaders become surreal meme characters, it's absurdist humor with zero policy content: just vibes, compression artifacts, and soda. Play it as a non-sequitur or a tribute to the deep-fried era of political memes.
origin: A deep-fried viral clip from the political-absurdism meme genre.

title: Aayein?!
blurb: AAYEIN?! — the legendary confused exclamation from Indian meme culture, powered by actor Paresh Rawal's perfect delivery. It's the desi internet's answer to 'excuse me?!': disbelief, offense, and demand for explanation in one syllable. Play it at nonsense of any origin. One of the great reaction sounds of the Indian meme renaissance.
origin: Paresh Rawal's iconic confused exclamation from Indian cinema, meme-ified.

title: Abhi Maza Aayega Na Bidu
blurb: 'Abhi maza aayega na bidu!' — now the fun begins. The gleeful Indian meme line announcing that the situation is about to get entertaining, usually at someone's expense. It's the desi equivalent of grabbing popcorn: play it when drama ignites in the group chat or a rematch is accepted. The anticipation is the celebration.
origin: The viral 'now it gets fun' line from Indian meme culture.

title: Bomboclat
blurb: BOMBOCLAT — the Jamaican patois exclamation that became a global meme, deployed for shock, emphasis, and moments beyond ordinary vocabulary. The internet adopted it as an all-purpose caption and reaction; the delivery carries a force that transcends translation. Use respectfully, use dramatically, and understand it means business.
origin: The Jamaican patois exclamation, adopted globally as a shock reaction.

title: French Meme Song
blurb: The French meme song — that jaunty accordion-adjacent tune that turns any clip into a Parisian comedy. The internet uses it for moments of Continental absurdity: mimes, baguettes, elegant failures, and anyone being dramatically European. It's a whole aesthetic in eight seconds. Oui oui, press the button.
origin: The jaunty tune of French-flavored meme edits.

title: Life Is Roblox (DJ Khaled)
blurb: 'Life is Roblox.' — DJ Khaled's accidental philosophy, from the interview moment where he compared existence to a children's block game and meant it completely. The internet enshrined it instantly: play it when reality glitches, when NPCs appear in daily life, or when the simulation shows its seams. He said what he said. Life is, in fact, Roblox.
origin: DJ Khaled's viral 'life is Roblox' interview moment.

title: Pluh
blurb: PLUH — the sound a cat allegedly makes when it has nothing further to add. This tiny absurdist syllable became a whole communication style: conversation over, thought complete, pluh. It's the brainrot era's period mark. Send it as a reply, an agreement, or an exit. There is nothing else to say. Pluh.
origin: The viral 'pluh' cat clip — the internet's conversation-ending syllable.

title: Fart with Reverb
blurb: The fart with reverb — the humble fart, promoted to cathedral acoustics. Adding reverb transforms a two-star joke into a cinematic event: it echoes, it lingers, it demands reflection. This is the fart for dramatic moments, slow-motion edits, and spaces with implied vaulted ceilings. Proof that production value improves everything.
origin: The classic fart, elevated by professional-grade reverb.

title: Can We Get Much Higher
blurb: CAN WE GET MUCH HIGHER — the soaring vocal from Kanye's 'Dark Fantasy', turned by edit culture into the sound of peak hype. It plays over anime power-ups, sports miracles, and any moment that ascends. The One Piece edits made it legendary; now anything climbing earns the vocal. For altitude of every kind, literal and emotional.
origin: The 'Dark Fantasy' vocal, canonized by One Piece and hype edits.

title: Acumalaka
blurb: ACUMALAKA — the chant that spread through TikTok like a spell nobody could stop casting. Part of the brainrot canon where sounds mean nothing and everything simultaneously, it's pure phonetic joy: fun to hear, funnier to say, impossible to explain to adults. Play it as a greeting, a victory cry, or an incantation. Acumalaka.
origin: A viral brainrot chant from TikTok.

title: Bye Bye (Mewing)
blurb: The 'bye bye' mewing sound — the audio for the shush-and-jawline gesture that swept TikTok. Someone asks a question, the finger goes to the lips, the jawline gets pointed at: can't talk, mewing. It's peak gesture-meme culture, and this clip is its voice. Play it to exit any conversation with maximum unserious discipline.
origin: From TikTok's mewing/shush gesture meme.

title: Sonic.EXE Scream
blurb: The Sonic.EXE scream — the distorted shriek from gaming's most infamous creepypasta, sibling to the laugh we also host. This is the jumpscare payload: corrupted, sudden, and engineered to ruin composure. Use it for horror edits, fake-outs, and the moment wholesome content turns cursed. Found footage energy from the haunted-cartridge era.
origin: The scream from the Sonic.EXE creepypasta games.

title: FNAF 2 Scream
blurb: The FNAF 2 jumpscare scream — the sequel's animatronic shriek, sharper and meaner than the original. Toy animatronics turned out to be nothing like toys, and this scream is the proof. Essential for horror edits, reaction-bait, and completing your Freddy's audio arsenal alongside the first game's scream. The night shift never gets easier.
origin: The jumpscare scream from Five Nights at Freddy's 2.

title: FNAF 4 Jumpscare
blurb: The FNAF 4 jumpscare — the nightmare animatronics' scream, widely rated the most terrifying in the series. FNAF 4 moved the horror into a child's bedroom and turned the volume of dread accordingly. This is the scream for maximum-impact scares: closer, louder, and meaner than anything before it. Sleep is canceled.
origin: The nightmare-animatronic jumpscare from Five Nights at Freddy's 4.

title: FNAF Yay! (Children)
blurb: The FNAF children's 'YAY!' — cheering kids, rendered deeply unsettling by context. In-game it celebrates; in your headphones at 2am it threatens. This clip is beloved for that exact duality: genuinely cheerful audio that FNAF lore made permanently ominous. Use it for wholesome moments, cursed moments, and wholesome moments about to become cursed.
origin: The children's cheer from Five Nights at Freddy's — innocent until context.

title: Clash of Clans Intro
blurb: The Clash of Clans startup — the war-horn fanfare that opened a billion sessions of village-checking. It's mobile gaming's most nostalgic three seconds: hearing it teleports an entire generation back to raid planning and builder anxiety. Play it before any strategic undertaking, from actual games to dividing the restaurant bill.
origin: The startup fanfare from Clash of Clans (Supercell).

title: Clash Royale King Laugh
blurb: The Clash Royale king's laugh in its clean, original form — the polished cousin of the deep-fried HE HE HE HA we also host. This is the version that actually taunts you in-game after every bridge-spam defeat. Play it post-victory for regulation-grade disrespect, or keep both versions loaded and escalate as needed.
origin: The king's laugh emote from Clash Royale, original quality.

title: Fortnite Knocked
blurb: The Fortnite knocked sound — the thud-and-groan of a player hitting the ground in crawl mode. Not dead, just profoundly humbled. It's the sound for partial defeats everywhere: the argument you lost but survived, the Monday you're crawling through. Someone can still revive you. Whether they will is the real battle royale.
origin: The player-knockdown sound from Fortnite.

title: Goku Yelling (Power Up)
blurb: Goku yelling — the sustained Super Saiyan charging scream that defined an entire genre of anime moment. Twenty seconds of pure effort before anything actually happens: it's commitment as content. Play it while opening a jar, waiting for a download, or summoning the will to reply to an email. The power level is rising. Eventually.
origin: Goku's iconic power-up scream from Dragon Ball Z.

title: Crowd Booing
blurb: A full crowd booing — stadium-scale disapproval on demand. The boo is democracy's oldest review system, and this crowd delivers it with conviction. Play it after bad puns, worse decisions, and anyone suggesting the meeting run long. The counterweight to our cheering crowd: same arena, opposite verdict. The people have spoken, negatively.
origin: Stadium crowd booing — mass disapproval, instantly.

title: DAMN
blurb: DAMN — the drawn-out exclamation that responds to roasts, reveals, and plot twists on behalf of everyone watching. It's the crowd reaction compressed into one voice: something just happened and it requires acknowledgment. Play it after burns land, secrets drop, or anyone gets told. The correct response to witnessed devastation since forever.
origin: The classic drawn-out 'DAMN' reaction.

title: Extremely Loud CORRECT Buzzer
blurb: The EXTREMELY LOUD correct buzzer — being right, at a volume that constitutes assault. The counterpart to our extremely loud incorrect buzzer: this one celebrates accuracy with the same total disregard for eardrums. Play it when someone nails the answer and deserves to have the entire street know. Correctness this loud cannot be appealed.
origin: The maximum-volume edition of the correct-answer buzzer.

title: Correct Ding
blurb: The correct ding — the crisp, civilized chime of a right answer. Where our loud buzzer screams correctness, this one simply confirms it: clean, satisfying, quiz-show official. Use it for trivia nights, teaching moments, and dignifying small daily victories. The gold star of sounds, ready for deployment at any act of being right.
origin: The classic right-answer chime of quiz culture.

title: Kids Cheering (Yay!)
blurb: Kids cheering YAY — unfiltered childhood celebration, the most sincere audio on Earth. It's the sound for wins that deserve pure joy rather than adult restraint: cake arriving, school canceling, the ice cream truck existing. Also devastating when used ironically over minor adult accomplishments. Either way, the kids are thrilled for you.
origin: Classic children's cheer — pure celebration.

title: Gunshot
blurb: A single clean gunshot crack — the standard-issue bang of action edits, western standoffs, and race starts. Editors need this constantly: it's punctuation for dramatic exits, startle cuts, and 'and then everything changed' moments. One shot, professionally sharp, no echo baggage. Handle your edits responsibly.
origin: A clean single gunshot for edits and dramatic punctuation.

title: Punch
blurb: The punch sound — a meaty cinematic impact that no real fist has ever produced. Movie punches sound like this because reality is disappointing; edits inherit the tradition. Use it for physical comedy, verbal knockouts, and moments where an argument lands like a haymaker. THWACK. The debate is over.
origin: The classic cinematic punch impact.

title: Bone Crack
blurb: The bone crack — a crisp skeletal crunch that makes entire rooms wince. It's the sound for stretches that go too well, falls that land wrong, and any physical event the viewer should feel personally. Sound designers know: the crack sells the injury. Deploy for sympathetic pain, chiropractic content, and full-body cringe.
origin: A crisp cartilage-and-bone crunch for maximum wince.

title: Swoosh
blurb: The swoosh — the air-slicing whoosh of fast movement and faster transitions. It's editing's most-used connective tissue: scene changes, text flying in, hands gesturing dramatically. Nothing physical needs to move for a swoosh to work; it creates the motion by itself. The duct tape of sound design, in premium quality.
origin: The classic transition whoosh.

title: Ear Ringing (Tinnitus)
blurb: The ear-ringing tone — that high, thin eeeeee of post-explosion cinema, flashbang aftermaths, and standing up too fast. Film grammar uses it for dazed disorientation, and edits inherited the trick: play it after loud chaos, overwhelming news, or your alarm's third snooze. The world goes distant, the ring takes over. Realistic enough to check your own ears.
origin: The cinematic post-blast ear ring.

title: Viking War Horn (Gjallarhorn)
blurb: The Gjallarhorn — the massive Viking war horn blast that summons battle energy from a thousand years ago. Popularized by Minnesota's stadium ritual, the sound outgrew football entirely: it's now the internet's horn for any epic mobilization. Play it before raids, road trips, and group orders arriving. SKOL. The horde is ready.
origin: The Viking war horn, famous from Minnesota's stadium tradition.

title: Ding
blurb: A single perfect ding — the atom of notification sounds. Bell-clear, instantly understood, infinitely applicable: idea arriving, elevator landing, order ready, point made. When a moment needs marking and nothing fancy will do, the ding does it. The most honest sound in the catalog: it dings. That's the whole feature set.
origin: One clean bell ding — the universal alert.

title: Door Knocking
blurb: Three firm knocks on a door — arrival announced the analog way. The knock is loaded with narrative: who is it, why now, do we answer? Play it in edits for incoming visitors, in calls to fake a mysterious guest, or behind someone wearing headphones for a jump-scare with plausible deniability. Knock knock. You're welcome.
origin: A firm triple door knock.

title: Instagram Thud
blurb: The Instagram thud — the weighty boom-tap of the app's notification, instantly recognized by a billion thumbs. It carries strange gravity: something happened, someone reacted, the algorithm has news. Use it in edits about posting, or play it aloud to trigger the collective phone-check. Social media's heartbeat, one thud at a time.
origin: Instagram's distinctive notification thud.

title: Grindr Notification
blurb: The Grindr notification — one of the most instantly recognized message sounds ever shipped, complete with everything its arrival implies. The meme usage thrives on context: played in public, it turns heads and starts conversations. Use it in edits for maximum implication, or as the boldest possible text tone. The sound speaks for itself. Loudly.
origin: Grindr's infamous message notification.

title: SpongeBob Disappointed
blurb: The SpongeBob disappointed sting — Bikini Bottom's official sound of hopes gently dying. Less catastrophic than the fail sting, more resigned than the boowomp: this is disappointment as weather, just passing through. Play it for unmet expectations of every size: empty fridges, canceled plans, seeing the group photo. The sea sympathizes.
origin: A disappointment sting from SpongeBob SquarePants.

title: SpongeBob Levitating
blurb: The SpongeBob levitating sound — the mystical hum from the meme where the sponge simply ascends. It's the audio for transcendence, sarcastic or otherwise: leaving your body during awkward conversations, achieving enlightenment via snacks, rising above drama both literally and spiritually. When the situation calls for departure from physics, press this.
origin: From the levitating SpongeBob meme — the sound of ascension.

title: Goofy Ahh SpongeBob
blurb: Goofy ahh SpongeBob — Bikini Bottom processed through the goofy ahh filter, where even a cartoon sponge gets more cartoonish. It's two comedy universes colliding: SpongeBob's chaos energy warped into brainrot's house style. Play it when regular SpongeBob sounds are somehow too dignified for the moment. Yes, that situation exists.
origin: SpongeBob audio, goofy-ahh-ified.

title: Goofy Ahh Baby
blurb: The goofy ahh baby — infant audio warped into the goofy ahh dimension, where even babies are unserious. It's chaotic, wrong, and inexplicably funny: the sound of the youngest generation already committed to the bit. Play it over baby content, childish adult behavior, and anyone's origin story. Born goofy, as the prophecy foretold.
origin: A baby clip from the goofy ahh meme genre.

title: Goofy Ahh Dora
blurb: Goofy ahh Dora — the explorer, deep-fried beyond map-reading capability. Childhood educational content processed into brainrot is a whole genre, and Dora is its patron saint: familiar enough to recognize, warped enough to disturb. Play it for millennial-childhood-ruined moments and expeditions going profoundly wrong. Swiper no swiping the audio quality.
origin: Dora the Explorer audio, goofy-ahh-ified.

title: Goofy Ahh Running
blurb: The goofy ahh running sound — cartoon sprint audio for the least dignified escapes. Those rubbery, frantic footsteps upgrade any chase into a circus: play it over people running for buses, dogs doing zoomies, and tactical retreats from responsibility. Nobody has ever looked cool while this sound played. That's the entire design goal.
origin: Cartoon sprint audio from the goofy ahh genre.

title: Discord Troll
blurb: The Discord troll sound — engineered specifically to disrupt voice chats. It's the audio equivalent of poking someone repeatedly: not harmful, deeply annoying, impossible to ignore. Load it into your server soundboard for maximum call chaos, or play it when someone's taking the game too seriously. Trolling responsibly is still trolling.
origin: A voice-chat disruption classic from Discord soundboard culture.

title: Nope.avi
blurb: Nope.avi — the TF2 Engineer's flat, final 'nope', star of one of YouTube's earliest immortal shitposts. It's refusal in its purest form: no explanation, no negotiation, just nope. Play it at requests, dares, Mondays, and anything else that deserves a one-word veto delivered in a Texas drawl. A founding document of meme audio.
origin: The Engineer's 'nope' from Team Fortress 2, immortalized by nope.avi.

title: Siren Head
blurb: The Siren Head sound — the distorted emergency-broadcast wail of the internet's favorite lanky cryptid. Trevor Henderson's creation speaks in corrupted siren tones, and this audio is its voice: wrong in a way that raises neck hair. Play it in the woods at your own risk, or use it for horror edits and ruining camping trips.
origin: The signature wail of Trevor Henderson's Siren Head cryptid.
